<STRUCT_0001>
Note that given a morphism <MATH_0001> in <MATH_0002> we get a
corresponding natural transformation of functors <MATH_0003>
defined by composing with the morphism <MATH_0004>. This turns
composition of morphisms in <MATH_0005> into composition of
transformations of functors. In other words we get a functor
<MATH_0006>
Note that the target is a ``big'' category, see
Remark <REF_0001>. On the other hand,
<MATH_0007> is an actual mathematical object (i.e.<SPACE_0001>a set), compare Remark
<REF_0002>.
